snippet.title: I Made ₹2 Crore Corpus... Then Everything Changed!
snippet.description:
Is ₹2 Crore enough to retire in India, especially for a middle-class family with home loan, child education, medical expenses and daily household costs?

In this real Indian middle-class retirement story, Abhijit Patra shares how he went from a farmer’s family and a ₹500/month scholarship to building a ₹2.3 Crore corpus through education, SIPs, teaching income and disciplined investing.

But this video is not just about becoming a crorepati.

It is about the real middle-class dream:
building a house for parents, buying your own home, clearing the home loan, planning for your child’s education, and finally reaching a point where money gives you time, health and freedom.

In this episode, we break down:

* Is ₹2 Crore enough to retire in India?
* How much retirement corpus does a middle-class family need?
* How he started with a ₹500 SIP
* How SIPs helped him build long-term wealth
* How he increased his SIP to ₹1 lakh/month
* Why he keeps 70% in equity and 30% in debt
* How he cleared his home loan using investments
* Why education was the biggest turning point in his life
* How he is planning for his son’s higher education
* Why financial freedom is not only about quitting work

This is a story for every Indian family trying to balance responsibilities, EMIs, children’s education, parents, retirement planning and financial freedom.

If you are wondering whether ₹2 Crore is enough for retirement, or how a middle-class person can build wealth through SIPs and discipline, this story will give you a practical and emotional perspective.

snippet.title: Gold's Pullback, a Hidden Debt Crisis, and the K-Shaped Economy | Michael Dehn - Total Metals
snippet.description:
In this conversation with Michael Dehn, Chairman of Total Metals Corp. (TSX-V: TT) (OTCQB: TTTMF) (FSE: O4N), we discuss the recent pullback in precious metals, why gold’s move higher still has not translated into broader economic confidence, and how a K-shaped economy is shaping both investor behavior and commodity markets. Michael explains why wealthier investors continue to move into gold and hard assets while much of the public remains stuck on the sidelines, and why political gamesmanship is adding even more noise to commodity prices.

We also get into Total Metals’ recent drill results from Electro, the company’s growing portfolio of gold and critical minerals projects, what makes Pick Lake and High Lake stand out, and what the next 12 months could look like as the company works toward bigger permits, more drilling, and stronger engagement with local First Nations. snippet.title: Why are these real gold coins different colors?
snippet.description:
Ever notice how the Canadian Gold Maple Leaf looks brighter and more yellow, while the South African Krugerrand has that deeper, almost copper tone?

Here’s why 👇

The Maple Leaf is .9999 pure gold (24k) no added metals, giving it that rich, vibrant yellow shine.
The Krugerrand is 22k gold mixed with copper making it more durable, but also giving it that slightly reddish hue.

Even though it’s not 24k, each 1 oz Krugerrand still contains a full 1 troy ounce of pure gold. The extra weight comes from the copper alloy.

Are you stacking for purity… or durability?

snippet.title: Can You Really Retire With ₹2 Crore?
snippet.description:
Most people spend their 20s chasing wealth.

Rahul spent his 20s making sure he would never experience poverty again.

After watching his father lose everything during a financial crisis, Rahul made himself one promise no matter what happened, his family would never have to go through that again.

Starting with a ₹5 LPA software job, he invested consistently, built a ₹3 crore corpus, and retired at just 32 years old.

But this isn't just another FIRE story.

It's about fear, responsibility, disciplined investing, calculating your retirement scientifically, and redefining what it means to be rich.

In this conversation, Rahul shares:
• Why he never wanted to become rich only financially secure
• How he built his investment portfolio from scratch
• The retirement calculation that changed his life
• Why he moved to Goa after retiring
• How financial independence helped him overcome the fear of losing his job
• What "retiring rich" actually means

If you're in your 20s or 30s wondering whether early retirement is possible or simply want to become financially independent this conversation is full of practical lessons.

snippet.title: Quitting Corporate Was The Best Decision Of My Life
snippet.description:
What happens when a successful corporate professional decides to leave a ₹36 LPA career and dedicate her life to helping women become financially independent?

In this episode of Wint Wealth, we meet Chitra, founder of Taliru Foundation, who left the corporate world after years of building her own financial security. Inspired by personal experiences and the struggles she witnessed around her, she started an initiative that trains women to become auto-rickshaw drivers and earn a sustainable income.

Today, hundreds of women who once earned ₹5,000–₹8,000 a month as housemaids and daily wage workers are earning ₹30,000–₹50,000 a month through auto driving. Many are single mothers, widows, or women facing financial hardship. Through skill training, financial literacy, and employment support, Taliru Foundation is helping them build confidence, dignity, and financial independence.

In this conversation, Chitra shares:
- Why she left a successful corporate career
- The role of financial planning in pursuing purpose
- How investing helped her take risks
- Why women need financial independence
- The challenges of building a non-profit
- The real stories of women whose lives changed through earning

If you're interested in personal finance, financial freedom, women empowerment, career transitions, social entrepreneurship, and inspiring life stories, this episode is for you.

Timestamp - 

00:00 – Why Women Need Financial Independence
Chitra explains poverty, women’s low workforce participation, and why earning money gives women confidence and dignity.

00:54 – Meet Chitra & Taliru Foundation
How Taliru Foundation trains women to become self-reliant auto-rickshaw drivers.

01:40 – Threat Calls & Resistance
Why people opposed women entering auto driving, a male-dominated space.

02:18 – Chandrakala’s Story
Her struggles before auto driving and how earning changed her life.

03:03 – Chitra’s Journey & Turning Point
Her childhood, first salary, ₹36 LPA career, family break, husband’s cancer diagnosis, and why she entered the social sector.

08:06 – How Women Earn ₹30K–₹50K/Month
How Taliru’s training helps women move from ₹5K–₹8K jobs to higher income through auto driving.

09:24 – Abhilasha’s Story
From dependence and loneliness to earning, confidence, respect, and supporting her son.

10:08 – Impact, Advice & Financial Planning
Chitra’s fear of failure, women saving money, paying school fees without loans, and why founders need their own corpus before entering the social sector.

12:41 – Her Current Corpus & Closing Thought
Chitra shares her family’s investment mindset, ₹1.5 crore+ retirement corpus, and why collective effort is needed for change.
